narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To demonstrate that vaccines remain effective at preventing hospitalization for most people across different age groups and vaccine brands.

units.meaning: Across all age groups, brands, and both months, reported hospitalization-prevention effectiveness remains high: the lowest table value is 83% and the highest is 97.5%.
accepted_routes: Effectiveness ranges from 83% to 97.5% across all shown groups.
The lowest reported value is 83%, and the highest is 97.5%.
Even the weakest age-brand-month combination is still 83% effective.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must make the overall minimum and maximum data points readable across the age-group, brand, and month values.
units.temporal_anchor: 'continue to do effectively for most people'
units.reviewer_question: Should the video state the overall high range/minimum to establish that effectiveness remains high?

units.meaning: Johnson & Johnson is the lowest-effectiveness brand in every age group and month; in August 65+ it is 83% versus Pfizer 89% and Moderna 94%.

basis.note: Johnson & Johnson series; lowest August 65+ value.

accepted_routes: J&J is consistently the least effective brand across the age groups and months.
For 65+ in August, J&J is 83% compared with Pfizer 89% and Moderna 94%.
The lowest brand series is Johnson & Johnson throughout.
units.visual_evidence_rule: All three brand series must be visible for each age group and month so the lowest brand can be compared.
units.temporal_anchor: 'across different age groups and vaccine brands' / 'for most people'
units.reviewer_question: Is the brand ranking—especially J&J as the lowest—required, or is it enough to show effectiveness remains high?

units.meaning: In August, 65+ is the lowest age group for every brand: Pfizer 65+ 89% vs 96.5% for 18-49 and 95.5% for 50-64; Moderna 65+ 94% vs 97.5% and 97%; J&J 65+ 83% vs 93.5% and 93%.
accepted_routes: By August, the 65+ group is lowest for each brand.
August 65+ values (Pfizer 89%, Moderna 94%, J&J 83%) are below the corresponding younger-group values.
The oldest age group has the weakest August effectiveness in every brand series.
units.visual_evidence_rule: For each brand, the August values for 18-49, 50-64, and 65+ must be visible and comparable.
units.temporal_anchor: the 'for most people' clause supported by age-group data
units.reviewer_question: Should the video explicitly call out the August age gradient, with 65+ lower in every brand?

units.meaning: From May to August, all three brands' 65+ values decline; Pfizer 65+ has the largest drop, from 95% to 89% (down 6 percentage points), while Moderna 65+ drops 97% to 94% (-3 points) and J&J 65+ drops 85% to 83% (-2 points).
accepted_routes: All 65+ series decline from May to August, with Pfizer falling the most (6 points).
Pfizer 65+ goes from 95% to 89%, Moderna 65+ from 97% to 94%, J&J 65+ from 85% to 83%.
The largest May-to-August drop is Pfizer 65+ at 6 percentage points.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The May and August endpoints for the 65+ group must be visible for each brand, or the change must be directly shown.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video highlight that 65+ effectiveness declines from May to August, especially Pfizer's 6-point drop?

units.meaning: By August, Moderna has the highest effectiveness in every age group: 18-49 is 97.5%, 50-64 is 97%, and 65+ is 94%.

basis.note: Johnson & Johnson series; lower than Moderna.
Johnson & Johnson series; lower than Moderna.
Johnson & Johnson series; lower than Moderna.

accepted_routes: Moderna is the top brand in August for all three age groups.
August Moderna values are 97.5%, 97%, and 94%, above Pfizer and J&J in each age group.
Moderna has the highest August effectiveness in 18-49, 50-64, and 65+.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The August values for all brands within each age group must be visible to confirm Moderna is highest.
units.temporal_anchor: 'across different vaccine brands' / the August endpoint
units.reviewer_question: Is Moderna being the August leader optional detail, or should it be required for brand comparison?

optional_valid: Pfizer 18-49 in May is tied for the highest value in the table at 97.5%.
Moderna 65+ in May is 97%, the highest 65+ May value.
J&J 50-64 rises from 88% in May to 93% in August, a +5 percentage-point change (93 - 88 = 5).
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims such as waning immunity, vaccine brand causing lower protection, or vaccines becoming unnecessary.
Population shares or counts of people/hospitalizations not present in the table.
Future months or extrapolation beyond May and August.
Claims that all people are protected, or that any group has 100% effectiveness.
Describing percentage-point declines as a percent decrease rather than a difference in percentage points.
notes: All cited numbers are table values in %, and differences are percentage-point arithmetic. The set separates overall level, age ordering, brand ranking, and May-to-August change.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
